plain.text: Jesus taught a large crowd from a boat. He told a story: A farmer scattered seed. Some fell on the path and birds ate it. Some fell on rocky ground; it sprang up but withered in the sun because it had no roots. Some fell among thorns, which choked it. But some fell on good soil and produced a big harvest, thirty, sixty or even a hundred times what was sown. "Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear."

Later, his followers asked about the stories. Jesus said that the secret of God's kingdom had been given to them, but to outsiders everything comes in stories (parables), so that, as Isaiah said, they look but do not see.

Jesus explained the story. The seed is God's word. Some people hear it, but Satan quickly takes it away. Some receive it with joy, but give up when trouble comes. Some let worries, riches and other desires choke it. But some hear the word, accept it and produce a great harvest.
Jesus said a lamp is not put under a bowl, but on a stand. Whatever is hidden will be brought into the light. "Pay attention to what you hear," he said. The measure you use will be used for you.
God's kingdom is like seed a man scatters. Night and day the seed grows, though he does not know how. First the stalk, then the head, then the full grain. When it is ripe, the harvest comes.

God's kingdom is also like a mustard seed, one of the smallest seeds. Yet it grows into one of the largest garden plants, and birds can rest in its shade. Jesus taught many things in stories like these, and explained everything to his disciples in private.

That evening, Jesus and his disciples crossed the lake in a boat. A fierce storm came, and waves broke over the boat. Jesus was asleep on a cushion. The disciples woke him: "Teacher, don't you care if we drown?" Jesus got up, told the wind and waves, "Quiet! Be still!" and everything became completely calm. He asked them, "Why are you so afraid? Do you still have no faith?" They were terrified and asked each other, "Who is this? Even the wind and the waves obey him!"

summary.bigIdea: God's kingdom grows from small beginnings, and Jesus has power even over the storm.
points: The parable of the sower shows different ways people respond to God's word.
God's kingdom grows quietly and surprisingly, like a seed.
Jesus calms a storm, and his disciples wonder who he really is.
summary.reflection: Which kind of soil best describes your heart right now? What might help God's word grow in you?
